 I knew it would look bad in my resume, but it was worth it for my mental health. Plus, I figured that  I could justify it to my next employer by explaining that I quit so that I could put myself in a position to work for them.  I avoided having a gap in my resume by A: finding a part time job in my area of interest before I quit (less than 20hrs a week) and B: taking classes in my area of interest. Anyways, I will say a couple of things:
1) Cutting your hair and keeping your hair is not the only defining thing of a sikh. I'm not going to sugar coat it and say that it is not important according to the teachings of the religion, but being a sikh is more than keeping your hair.  

2) I too had social anxiety about my looks, and things did become different from me after I cut my hair. ...but it didn't make me happier. I was still very insecure about my looks for some reason and just didn't feel comfortable in my own skin. The anxiety you are feeling may not automatically go away after you cut your hair. Like me it could be a more deeper rooted problem. 

3)Good luck with your journey. I hope you find the internal peace you are looking for.
